name: Manufactured / mobile home community
summary: Land-lease community of HUD-code manufactured-home pads. The baseline cost is horizontal: private streets, water/sewer/storm, electric distribution, pads with hookups, landscaping and common amenities. The homes themselves are an optional line item. Per-pad cost is very sensitive to scale, because fixed infrastructure is spread over the pad count; the Anchorage study halves per-unit site cost going from 20 to 40 units. Cost also depends on whether public utilities are at the boundary. The only public per-pad budgets found are small, high-cost projects (Vermont, Alaska), so the national default is derived downward for scale and region. Home prices are solid (Census MHS).

typicalSize.method: Pads per community. Anchorage's existing stock: 12 large communities averaging ~300 units and 26 small ones averaging ~35 (e2). New greenfield communities are typically 100–250 pads to spread fixed infrastructure. Judgment for the mid.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Gross density incl. streets, open space and clubhouse. Typical zoning allows ~5–8 homes/acre for multi-section homes. Judgment; no source found this session.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Two-car driveway or carport pad per home (the Plainfield budget includes a driveway per lot, e1) plus guest parking. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per pad, horizontal infrastructure only (no home), incl. GC general conditions and OH&P, excl. contingency. Evidence (2025$): Plainfield VT 45-lot community expansion (e1): infrastructure $49,111 + sitework $20,000 + landscaping/amenities $13,111 + pad/slab/hookups/driveway $667 + general conditions $7,530 + contractor markup $15,959 ≈ $106k/lot. Anchorage AK feasibility study (e2): site preparation of $91,750/unit for a 40-unit and $183,500/unit for a 20-unit community. Both are small projects in high-cost, difficult-site markets (Vermont wetlands/flood relocation; Alaska), so they set the HIGH end ($110k). Mid $65k assumes a 100–150 pad greenfield community with public utilities at the boundary: Plainfield's $106k with fixed costs spread over ~3× the pads (Anchorage shows ~50% per-pad reduction when the pad count doubles; a ~30% scale reduction is assumed here) and ~10% regional normalization (106k × 0.7 × 0.9 ≈ $67k, rounded to $65k). Low $35k is a Sun Belt expansion phase reusing existing roads and plant; it sits above the $10–20k/unit infrastructure-replacement cost for existing parks in Minnesota (e3). The scale and regional factors are judgments; verify.

scope.notes: Per-pad share of internal streets and paving, earthwork, water/sewer/storm mains and laterals, electric distribution and pedestals, concrete pads/runners and driveways, landscaping, mailboxes and modest common-area amenities, incl. GC general conditions and OH&P. Excludes land, the manufactured home and its transport/installation (see line items), off-site utility extensions, lift stations/treatment plants, a clubhouse building, impact/tap fees and soft costs.

qualityTiers.method: Economy = low/mid (35/65 ≈ 0.54), tempered to 0.65 because economy communities still need code-minimum utilities. Premium/luxury (55+ resort-style communities with curb and gutter, underground utilities and larger pads) are judgment, with luxury ≈ the high/mid ratio (110/65 = 1.7).

systemSplit.method: From the Plainfield VT budget (e1), per lot: infrastructure (water/wastewater/storm/electric) $49,111, split 75% to Div 33 and 25% to Div 26 (electric), an assumption; sitework (excavation/grading/undergrounding/paving) $20,000, split 50/50 to 31 and 32; landscaping and amenities $13,111 to 32; general conditions plus 17.5% contractor markup to 01. Div 03 was raised from Plainfield's $667 (pad replacement only) to ~5% for new concrete pads/runners and driveways on every site. Then normalized to 1.000.

lineItems.name: New manufactured home (HUD-code), dealer price

cost.method: Census Manufactured Housing Survey, May 2026 average sales price (e4): single-section $82,200 (low), all homes $130,500 (mid), double-section $166,600 (high).

lineItems.notes: Switch on when the developer buys homes for sale or rent (community-owned rental homes). Excludes land.

lineItems.name: Home transport, installation, foundation/tie-downs, utility hookup and skirting

cost.method: Anchorage study uses $20,000 shipping per home (e2), which includes long-haul from the Lower 48 and sets the high end. The lower-48 mid/low are judgment for regional delivery, set-up crew, piers/anchors, hookups, skirting and steps. Census MHS price scope does not state whether delivery/setup is included, so this is carried separately; verify against dealer quotes.
Judgment: 1,500–5,000 SF clubhouse at ~$200–400/SF, plus a pool in resort-style communities. No source found.

lineItems.name: Sewer lift station

cost.method: Judgment for a packaged duplex-pump station sized for 100–300 homes. Verify with civil engineer.

lineItems.notes: Where gravity sewer to the public main is not possible.

pctOfHard.method: Plainfield VT budget per lot (e1): civil engineering $10,667 + other design $2,000 + survey $1,667 + permits $889 + legal $333 + environmental/NEPA/archaeology ~$311 + loan fees, inspection, interest and insurance $1,356 + marketing $667 ≈ $17,900. That is ~17% of the ~$106k pre-contingency hard cost. Adding owner project management ($12,000/lot) brings it to ~28% (high). Mid 18%. Low assumes larger scale and a simpler permitting path. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 1 point to remove loan fees and interest in the Plainfield budget. The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Civil engineering dominates; there is little building architecture. Utility tap/impact fees per pad vary widely and are not included.

design.method: Plainfield budget carries a 12% design/estimating contingency (e1), the high end. Mid 10% (judgment) once the civil design is advanced.

hard.method: Plainfield carries a 15% construction contingency (e1) on a wetlands/flood-relocation site, the high end. Mid 10% for typical greenfield sites (judgment).

soft.method: Plainfield soft cost contingency 8% (e1) used as the mid.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Per pad, hard + soft, excl. land and home. Min ≈ low $35k × 1.12. Max ≈ the Anchorage 20-unit site prep of $183,500 (e2) plus soft cost.

source.title: East Village Expansion — Proposed Grant Budget (CDBG-DR), 9/25/2025

evidence.quote: Infrastructure - W/WW/SW/Elect 2,210,000 49,111 This aligns with industry standards for per lot infrastructure construction; Sitework ... 900,000 20,000; Landscaping & site ammenities 590,000 13,111
evidence.scopeNotes: 45-lot manufactured-home community expansion (flood-recovery relocation). Value computed by the researcher: infrastructure + sitework + landscaping/amenities + pad/driveway ($667) + general conditions ($7,530) + 17.5% contractor markup ($15,959) per lot. Excludes the 12% design and 15% construction contingencies, owner's rep, demolition and the home line. Total hard construction is $144,359/lot including those items; total development cost is $222,368/lot.

openQuestions: No large-scale greenfield per-pad budget was found. REIT disclosures (Sun Communities, ELS, UMH expansion-site costs) or state HFA-funded new MHC budgets would replace the derived mid. Web search budget ran out before these could be checked.
Units per acre is unsourced; zoning-code minimum lot sizes for MH parks in several states would anchor it.
Whether Census MHS prices include delivery and installation should be confirmed from the questionnaire (cmh9a).
